doc: Work in progress. From a topological_offset construction (a .vtu, or a .msh with corr_input_vid), thins the offset band around the solid to a target thickness and, with prism_dominant, rebuilds it as prisms, pyramids and tets.

Build rods from original-correspondence offset regions collapsed to vertex rings. Equalize degrees along each path and map matching transported material slots. Construct adjacent-ring prism layers atomically, swap exterior interfaces when needed, and connect retained background through pyramids. Preserve input volume, shell reconstruction and protected attachment stars; invalid layers retain tets. Requires explicit input labels and correspondence.

Edge-based rod construction from complete source-edge tet links (requires rod_mode), including mixed shell/rod/solid inputs. Separate shared frame cofaces by conforming edge splits, insert midpoint sections and reselect the rod domain. Align ring degrees and fix material mapping before optimizing positions in the tet rod volume, then attempt interface swaps and native prism construction. Input points and refined joint stars stay fixed; failed layers retain tets. Reports include band-volume changes. Classify maximal edges without input-face or solid cofaces as rods. Separate shell-owned link points while retaining shell correspondence. Build and optimize shell cells first, then protect them during rod geometry and reconstruction. Existing vertex-region construction remains the default.

Edge-based rod mode only. Position-optimization sweeps on the tetrahedral rod volume after degree alignment and fixed ring mapping, before interface swaps and native prism construction. Zero disables these sweeps. Input points and protected joint stars remain fixed; all incident background tets must stay positive.

Nonnegative weight of radius and mapped circular-section targets relative to mean tet AMIPS during rod_position_iterations. Every valid prism-cap ring, including transition rings, targets every radial edge k at angle 2*pi*k/degree in its transported frame. Geometry errors are normalized by rod_radius. Zero performs AMIPS-only position optimization.

Optional surface fairing in the pre-prism rod tet position optimization. Penalizes longitudinal second differences of mapped radial vectors after parallel transport and deviations from regular circular ring spacing. Input centerline, joint offsets, ring mapping and tet connectivity stay fixed. Radius/section fitting and tet AMIPS remain active. Zero preserves the position optimizer without this fairing term.

Extra surface-smoothing sweeps after the existing rod tet position optimization, enabled only when rod_position_smoothing_weight is positive. Mapping and connectivity remain fixed. Neighboring pure-background interior vertices can relax with the rod surface; outer boundary, input and protected joint offsets stay fixed.

Radius/section-plane fitting weight in the optional second rod surface-smoothing pass. The original rod_position_weight and original position pass are preserved. Angular sliding is available to longitudinal/circular fairing while ring mapping stays fixed.

Edge-based rod mode: Laplace energy of rod vertices outside valid prism-cap rings. Offset-front vertices use surface neighbors and retain a carrier-radius penalty; every edge of every valid ring follows the globally transported material-slot targets. Input and protected joints remain fixed, and all incident tets must stay positive.

Optional geometry-only optimization of pure-rod branching joint offset stars, after regular rod positions and before background remeshing/native construction. In [0,200]; zero disables. Keep input graph, frame labels and all tet connectivity. Refresh the protected coordinate snapshot only after validating accepted joint moves.
Nonnegative surface Laplace energy weight for the optional joint pass, including joint port-ring points. All coupled rod/background tet AMIPS and radius/frame fitting remain active.

Nonnegative weight of radius-normalized carrier-radius and transported port-frame errors in the optional joint pass. Joint offsets have no cumulative displacement cap; geometry energy and energy-decreasing backtracking govern moves, and all incident tets must stay strictly positive.

Joint-core capsule-union smooth-min blend width divided by rod radius, in [0,1]. Zero gives the sharp tube union. Only joint-core points use this implicit reference; valid port rings retain their transported frame targets.

Alternate local background remeshing and a simultaneous rod/joint/background position solve, before native reconstruction. In [0,3]; zero retains the original single background-remeshing stage. Requires rod_edge_based and rod_background_remeshing with background present. Input graph, material mapping, neighborhood outer boundary, and rod tet connectivity stay fixed.
Joint rod/background position sweeps after each local remeshing round, in [1,200]. All affected tets remain strictly positive and each accepted step decreases combined energy.
Nonnegative shared surface Laplace weight across all rod offset points, including mapped frame rings and joint/tet regions, in each coupled round.

Nonnegative radius/frame fitting weight in each coupled round. Geometry targets and material mapping are retained; background points in the full surface-distance neighborhood can adapt to moving rod points.

Edge-based rods with background only. After rod position optimization, apply TetWild split/collapse/swap/smoothing to a local pure-background neighborhood, then run rod interface swaps and prism/pyramid construction. Rod cells/vertices and the extracted patch boundary remain fixed. No CDT is used.

Nonnegative outward distance from the actual rod surface in mesh coordinate units. Zero uses rod_radius. Select background tets with at least one vertex within this distance; fix patch boundary and existing points farther away.
Nonnegative TetWild target edge length at the rod surface, graded up to twice this value at the neighborhood boundary. Zero uses rod_radius.
Number of local split/collapse/swap/smooth passes, in [1,20], subject to the time limit and a 2000-split budget.
Positive time budget in seconds for rod-local background remeshing. A current operation and final validation can finish beyond the limit; accepted valid work is retained.
Rod mode only. Absolute target section radius; positive, or zero to use thicknessratio times the mean centerline edge length. Infeasible circular targets retain valid geometry and are reported.
Application name must be prismatic_mesh.
Construction .vtu or Gmsh 4.1 .msh with corr_input_vid. MSH can derive labels and cell tags from the tag_0/offset/ambient physical groups; explicit PRISM fields are also supported.
Output .vtu or .msh (Gmsh 4.1 ASCII) filename, relative to the JSON directory. A missing extension becomes .vtu.
Base directory for input; set by wmtk_app to the JSON directory.
Positive target thickness relative to the mean length of unique input surface edges.
Number of construction collapse/target-smoothing iterations. Zero computes targets without this construction optimization stage; quality_improvement has independent cycle and smoothing settings.

Keep exterior background tetrahedra during optimization/output. Background must remain strictly positive. Without background_remeshing only offset vertices move. Targets are computed from the band alone.

Explicitly discard background tetrahedra before rod preprocessing and joint optimization. Keep input volume and offset band, remove background constraints and background-pyramid reconstruction, and do not reattach the discarded mesh. Overrides keep_background_mesh. Intended for a band-only result or a background-constraint comparison.

After optimization, reconstruct conforming prisms, input-apex shell pyramids and tetrahedra. Retained background receives kernel-point pyramids in feasible disjoint quad-diagonal edge-star cavities. Preserve existing points, input volume and non-cavity background; fall back to conforming tet regions on failed geometry, overlap or search limits.
Additionally export the union of input volume and offset band as <output_stem>_input_shell.msh and .vtu, using the same final coordinates, hybrid cells and attributes while omitting background cells.

Optional nonnegative signed-volume floor for new or modified shell tetrahedra, candidate pyramid decompositions and new background pyramid cavity cones. The default zero requires strictly positive volume using exact predicates, without a coordinate-scale-dependent cutoff. Background optimization and unchanged background tets also require strictly positive volume.
Maximum smoothing step halvings after the full target step; between 0 and 60.
Optional prism Jacobian smoothing rounds after tet optimization. Zero disables this stage. Only offset vertices move; input, correspondence and connectivity remain fixed.

Optional fraction in [0,1). Each collapse or smoothing move must retain more than this fraction of every modified surviving tet's volume, including background. Zero keeps the original strict-positive rule. Deleted collapse cells are excluded. The absolute band min_tet_volume floor still applies.

Optional local convex-envelope initialization and concave-hinge smoothing after hybrid construction, in [0,100]. Only outer offset vertices in protected/marked transition neighborhoods move. Input, correspondence, connectivity and completed rod-prism frames stay fixed; every step checks reference tets, native prism/pyramid Jacobians and native shape quality. Zero disables this stage.

Optional final coupled offset smoothing rounds, in [0,200]. Fits shell normal offset distance and rod section radius/plane while improving native prism AMIPS. Neighboring free rod offsets may move together. Input and protected offset vertices, correspondence and connectivity stay fixed. Tets and pyramids supply positivity constraints only; their shape quality is not optimized. Zero disables this stage.
Positive target det(J), normalized by twice input triangle area times initial mean column length.
Positive quadratic weight on displacement from the position before Jacobian smoothing, normalized by target thickness (initial column length if unavailable).
Positive per-move displacement bound relative to thickness. Implemented with an inscribed axis-aligned box.
Positive total displacement bound from the position before Jacobian smoothing, relative to thickness. Implemented with an inscribed axis-aligned box.

Enable adaptive background 2-3/3-2 swaps and interior relaxation after each tet iteration, then retry collapse. Requires keep_background_mesh=true. Input/offset vertices and exterior boundary are fixed during remeshing.
Local remeshing passes per tet iteration; positive.
Trigger on background mean ratio below this threshold in (0,1]; 1 is a regular tet, 0 is degenerate. Background-blocked collapses are also repair targets.
Maximum accepted background swaps/moves per tet iteration; positive.
Maximum attempted background swaps/moves per tet iteration; positive.

Enable post-build region remeshing and native AMIPS-plus-thickness smoothing. Requires prism_dominant and a positive target thickness for the shell stage. With rod_mode, reserve rod tets/frames during shell optimization, then run dedicated rod geometry and construction while completed shell cells remain fixed. Replaces the separate Jacobian/background quality stages and transition/thickness smoothing. False disables this postprocess; there is no legacy relocation fallback. Nonzero min_tet_volume or relative_tet_volume_floor are rejected: this stage enforces strict positivity of actual cells.

Options for quality_improvement. Final output selects the valid stage with the lowest combined AMIPS, point-height and neighbor-height energy. Convergence requires both the quality and enabled thickness criteria; finite budgets do not guarantee these targets. Non-box exterior domains retain fixed source triangulation, including offset boundaries if background was removed.

Maximum outer cycles, in [0,100]. Each has mixed smoothing, native/surface operations, bulk tet remeshing and mixed smoothing. Subsequent cycles halve sizing in one-ring neighborhoods of mixed cells above quality_target.

Maximum gradient smoothing sweeps per mixed stage, in [0,10000]. Active vertices come from actual mixed cells above quality_target and enabled point/neighbor height errors above thickness_tolerance. Stop when no move is accepted or both criteria are met.
Tet optimizer pass pairs per outer cycle, in [0,100]. Interfaces are fixed during this bulk stage.
Maximum paired prism-column collapse attempts per cycle; nonnegative.
Maximum conforming mixed surface/native split transactions per cycle; nonnegative.
Maximum compatible input/prism cap swaps per cycle; nonnegative.
Maximum generated interior tet split vertices per bulk stage; nonnegative. Unrepresentable floating-point midpoints are rejected.
Positive soft time limit in seconds, checked between operations. Validation and export may extend beyond it.
Positive multiplier of the initial mean unique offset-face edge length. The target length and adaptive refinement floor are clamped to the nominal thickness.
Raw native AMIPS stopping/activation threshold, finite and greater than 3; ideal=3. Covers all actual tet/prism/pyramid cells including input volume and background.
Threshold of the squared excess AMIPS loss; at least 3 and strictly below quality_target. The loss includes a small log-AMIPS regularizer.

Nonnegative weight on squared differences of relative reference-height errors across neighboring shell-interface vertices. Degree-normalized pairs exclude opposite reference normals, normal changes above thickness_feature_angle and target-height ratios above 1.5. Zero disables this term.

Positive finite activation and convergence tolerance for relative reference-height error and neighbor error differences; 0.05 means 5%. Each criterion applies only when its energy weight is positive. Vertices without a valid reference on a shell interface are held fixed during mixed smoothing and counted in the report.
Reference-normal angle in degrees, in (0,90], above which neighboring interface vertices are not coupled by thickness smoothing. Does not add a geometry envelope or change input feature constraints.

Nonnegative weight on squared relative projection-height error along the original reference direction. thickness_smoothing_weight controls the neighbor term separately. The projection band is max(25%, current error). Zero disables point-height activation and energy.
Enable native/surface and bulk tetrahedral topology operations; false runs the mixed smoothing stages alone.
